newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices stable amid Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices stable amid Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. stock index options trading was steady, if uneventful, as Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan was testifying before the U.S. House of Representatives, traders said Wednesday.
"The pit is relatively quiet today," one S&P 500 .SPX options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "There's not a lot of shooting going on here."
In the second half of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, Greenspan repeated his comments to the Senate last week and traders were focusing next on the question and answer segment of his testimony.

The market rallied in the face of Greenspan's comments, with March S&P 500 futures up 7.15 at 799.20 at around 1345 CST/1945 GMT. The index reached a session peak of 800.90 shortly after Greenspan began his testimony.
The spot SPX index was up 6.63 at 797.58.
Earlier, one firm pegged March fair value at 1.10 points premium to cash, with buy programs at a 2.35-point premium or wider and sell programs at a 0.30-point premium or narrower.

"We did a little stuff this morning but really it has been pretty slow all day and I think it's mainly because people are waiting for Greenspan to say what he's going to say," the head of one options trading desk in Chicago said.
He added that once Greenspan is out of the way, investors and traders will focus on Friday's February employment report, which could keep activity under wraps through Thursday.
The trader at the CME said most of the activity was from locals mainly exiting positions, but he said one institution was fairly active in the March 730 puts.
The trader added that investors were beginning to take a look at April options. March contracts expire in about two weeks.
Among SPX options traded at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, activity remained centered on the put side, led by the March 790 puts, which traded 6,605 contracts.
The March 795 put traded about 2,655. On the call side, the March 810 traded nearly 2,100.
In the April series, the 875 call traded about 4,400 contracts at prices ranging from one to 1-1/4. The 865 call traded 2,350 contracts.
Also in the April series, the 780 put traded about 2,980 contracts and the 800 call and 730 put each traded about 1,010 contracts.
Among OEX March puts, activity was solid from the 745 strike through the 780 strike. March calls were busy from the 770 strike through the 835 strike.
Farther out, the April 840 call traded about 6,920 contracts and the June 780 put traded about 2,400.
